attacks.claim: The chosen Starter tier (5 req/min, 15-min delayed quotes) cannot support the chain_poller design, which needs 160 req/min of real-time polling for 40 underlyings. The data feed fails almost immediately, and the intraday triggers would run on stale quotes.
attacks.evidence: "chain_poller (new): every 15 s, fetch a real-time option chain snapshot ... 40 underlyings => 160 requests/min during RTH." / "We stay on Starter." / Starter "5 req/min | 15-min delayed"

attacks.claim: The $250/month cap is not met once the design is made feasible. Only Growth ($199) meets the rate limit with real-time quotes, and Growth plus the $60 VPS totals $259, over the cap. The $139 figure rests on the infeasible Starter tier.
attacks.evidence: "Monthly run cost: Optiq Starter $79 + existing VPS $60 = $139, comfortably inside the $250 cap."

attacks.claim: Migration 0042 drops roll_history in production in the same transaction as a 90-day backfill, with no backup, snapshot, down-migration, or verification step. Older history is irreversibly lost, and the stated fallback (roll_eod.py behind ROLLER_V2=false) likely reads the dropped column, so the rollback path is broken by the migration itself.
attacks.evidence: "Migration 0042 runs in-place against prod Monday 08:00 ET" / "In the same transaction, ALTER TABLE positions DROP COLUMN roll_history." / "roll_eod.py stays deployed behind ROLLER_V2=false as the fallback path through week 4." / ABSENT: backup, down-migration, restore procedure.

attacks.claim: Discarding trade and roll records older than 90 days may breach record-retention obligations for a managed family-office account (tax lot and cost-basis reporting, regulatory records). The plan does not verify that nothing else depends on the older entries.
attacks.evidence: "Backfill copies roll_history entries from the last 90 days into rolls; older entries are not needed by roll_engine." / ABSENT: retention policy or archive of removed history.

attacks.claim: Automated, high-frequency options order submission (up to 8 roll orders per day, repriced every 20 s up to 3 times) has no stated review against broker API terms, order-rate rules, or supervisory sign-off for automated trading.
attacks.evidence: "order_router ... re-priced every 20 s up to 3 times, then cancelled." / ABSENT: broker ToS review or supervisory controls.

attacks.claim: Vendor option snapshots can drive live orders with no freshness, sanity, or schema validation. The heartbeat guard covers only broker connectivity, so stale or malformed quotes can produce wrong rolls.
attacks.evidence: "roll_engine stops emitting intents when the last successful broker heartbeat is > 60 s old." / ABSENT: any freshness or validity check on chain_poller snapshots.

attacks.claim: Kill-switch and partial-state behavior are undefined. ROLLER_KILL is read per loop, but the plan does not say what happens to in-flight or repricing combo orders on kill, or how a filled buy-to-close with a rejected sell-to-open or a failed cancel is handled. Partial exposure is possible.
attacks.evidence: "plus a ROLLER_KILL env switch read on every loop." / "combo orders are all-or-none at the broker; a rejected combo leaves the original short call untouched." / ABSENT: in-flight order handling on kill and cancel-failure behavior.

attacks.claim: Daily order limits have no stated persistence, so a restart could reset counters and bypass the 1-per-contract and 8-per-account caps. There is no alerting or monitoring for a runaway loop. The limits also do not account for combo retries and lack an idempotency key against duplicate submits.
attacks.evidence: "order_router enforces max 1 roll per contract per day and max 8 roll orders per account per day; both are hard limits checked before submit" / ABSENT: counter persistence, alerting, idempotency keys.

attacks.claim: Optiq Data is the sole decision input with no fallback feed, exit plan, or rate-limit/backoff handling. A rate-limit breach would silently starve the trigger engine.
attacks.evidence: "Current vendor: Optiq Data." / ABSENT: alternate source, backoff logic, contract exit terms.

attacks.claim: The +3.8% net APR headline is unsupported: no backtest, prototype, or cost model, only anecdotal desk notes. The 30-day success window cannot separate the effect from market-regime noise, and the paper-mode comparison runs on delayed quotes so it cannot validate fills.
attacks.evidence: "Expected impact: +3.8% net APR vs. EOD rolling (see §2)." / "Desk notes from the last two quarters list several days where a mid-session roll 'would have been better'." / "Week 2-3: paper mode ... compare intents vs. EOD decisions daily."

attacks.claim: Trigger and target definitions are ambiguous: extrinsic is not specified as mid or last, and 'credit' for the strike-up rule is not defined net of buyback.
attacks.evidence: "DTE <= 5 and extrinsic value < $0.10" / "next strike up if the credit is >= $0.05"
